decision: Build with zero external dependencies (Node node:sqlite + node:http).
rationale: Matches the Command Center's zero-dep ethos; durable store needed anyway; avoids supply-chain surface for shared infrastructure.

decision: Cortex talks to Ollama's native API, not the local_llm :8000 wrapper.
rationale: The wrapper pins a fixed global num_ctx=16384 and its OpenAI surface hides prompt_eval_count. Cortex needs per-call num_ctx and evaluated-token counts to enforce the floor and prove no truncation.

decision: Vendor retail-search NDCG verbatim (with SHA drift check) rather than reimplement or cross-import.
rationale: Gen-0 found it textbook-correct; a second divergent NDCG is the plausible-wrong-number risk; a relative cross-repo path breaks silently.

decision: Default provider order Gemini->OpenRouter->local (configurable), pending OQ-1.
rationale: Matches MISSION.md:32 and the Command Center's live config. MISSION.md:45 'local-first' contradicts this; local is retained as the always-available floor. Ferosh owns the final order.

decision: Fairness floor default: a job-call every 4th dispatch, pending OQ-4.
rationale: 'Jobs must not starve' needs a number to be testable. 25% of dispatch slots guarantees progress. Ferosh owns the number.

decision: Relevance grading scale 0-3 graded (2^g-1 gain), pending OQ-5.
rationale: Conventional pairing with retail-search's default; nothing in ecommmerce-eval constrains it yet.

decision: Do NOT build a full OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions surface tonight.
rationale: Third-person review flagged it as retrofit friction (GAP-1). Building it silently would expand scope; the caller flattens messages per HANDOFF.md. A compatibility shim is surfaced to Ferosh as a possible Gen-2, not assumed.

decision: Capture provider stop-reason (done_reason/finish_reason) and diagnose output-side truncation as a caller-budget fault; does not trigger fallback.
rationale: A thinking model (qwen3:4b) at a small maxTokens burns the whole completion budget on <think> and returns HTTP 200 with empty output and done_reason=length; Cortex previously surfaced only a generic parse failure, forcing the operator to hypothesize truncation. Recording it turns a guess into a fact and points at the caller's token budget, not the prompt/model. Additive+idempotent schema migration verified on the live 1,329-row DB.

decision: Adopt ecommmerce-eval's validated judge system prompt (MEASUREMENT NOTATION + PRODUCT TYPE sections).
rationale: Independently reproduced on live llama3.2:3b: the judge read cosmetic notation (1/2-in vs 1/2 in.) as a size mismatch and graded relevant products 0 with a spurious 'incorrect size unit' reason, inconsistently, contaminating notation-equivalence queries. Applied the byte-identical validated prompt; re-validated here (notation defect resolved, 13/13 deterministic, product-type discrimination preserved). Fix is Cortex's own JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT, so in scope.

decision: Judge prompt is COMPOSED: Cortex owns the structural frame (0-3 scale + one-line-JSON contract); callers may supply an optional domain `rubric` via POST /v1/relevance. Not a raw full-prompt override.
rationale: The rubric is domain knowledge (e.g. '#8 = No. 8 gauge' is a fact about a hardware catalogue, not about LLM execution); baking every such rule into Cortex couples its release cycle to one client's prompt tuning and cannot serve a second catalogue. The frame stays non-overridable so the scale/parse invariants that make a grade trustworthy survive (a client 0-10 scale would mass-fail parseJudgment). Full composed prompt is captured per trace as before; rubric_hash gives a version id. Default rubric = the ecommmerce text, byte-identical to prior deploy, so existing behaviour is unchanged. Resolves eval-reports' friction (guidelines/instructions fields were previously ignored).

decision: Read-through cache for relevance judgments, keyed on hash(composed prompt + rubric_hash + params + judge-model-scope). Call-level, serves both standalone and job calls; scoped to deterministic relevance judgments, not live routing calls.
rationale: Judgments are temp-0 deterministic, so a repeat is the SAME grade, not an approximation; a re-run after a ranking/pipeline change is almost all hits because judgments are rank-independent, turning a 60s+/pair batch into ms. Key includes rubric_hash + model scope so a rubric tweak or model swap MISSES (guards MISSION.md:93 stale-confident-number). Provenance preserved: a served grade keeps source_trace_id and is auditable in the viewer; only succeeded/parseable grades are cached (a bad run is never frozen). fresh:true bypasses; POST /v1/admin/prune {cache:true} clears after in-place model update.

decision: Dashboard shows a windowed Jobs count and a Served-from-cache measure.
rationale: Ferosh could not see this-morning's eval jobs: the data was present (231 job-calls, correct in /v1/metrics) but Command Center's live calls (every ~2min) fill the 15-row Recent-calls list, pushing 12h-old job-calls off, and there was no jobs-in-window aggregate. Added jobs_in_window + a cache hit measure to summary() and the strip; dashboard already auto-refreshes every 3s.

decision: Viewer ?job= deep-link scopes to that job only (server-side job_id filter on /v1/traces), with a back-link to full activity.
rationale: A deep link was fetching all 200 recent traces and merely expanding the target job, so a job link dumped the whole tree. Added a job filter to listTraces + /v1/traces?job=; viewer fetches only that job's calls. Verified: scoped returns exactly the job's 145 calls vs 200 unscoped. Also pruned all test-client data (allowlist: cache-demo/cache-verify/deploy-verify*/x/replay/test/cc/determinism) leaving only ecommmerce-eval, command-center, mde-control-center; cleared the demo judgment cache.

decision: Add GET /v1/jobs (paginated jobs list from the jobs table) + a viewer Jobs/All-activity toggle; jobs listed from the jobs table, not derived from the recent-traces feed.
rationale: Ferosh could not see submitted eval jobs because the viewer/dashboard build their views from the most-recent-N calls, which live Command Center traffic (or one large job) fills entirely, and there was no pagination. Reading the jobs table directly with limit/offset means jobs are always listable regardless of call volume. Newest-first with a rowid tiebreaker for same-ms submits; each row shows counts incl. served_from_cache so fully-cached jobs never look empty.

decision: Surface judgment-cache size on the dashboard + a Clear-cache button (reusing the two-step-confirm prune control); cache clear already available via POST /v1/admin/prune {cache:true}.
rationale: Ferosh worried about cache disk growth. Added est_bytes to judgmentCacheStats and a Trace Store line 'N entries · est size' plus a clear button. Real numbers: 226 entries = 44 KB of a 53 MB DB (0.08%); ~200 bytes/entry over a finite query×product space, so it cannot balloon. Clearing only forces deterministic re-judging.

decision: Home-page 'Recent calls' becomes a filterable, paginated Calls grid (debugging surface); /v1/traces gains offset + filters (type/status/provider/client/purpose/free-text q) and returns {total,limit,offset,traces}; new /v1/facets for filter dropdowns.
rationale: Ferosh: 'pagination is a must if I cannot see all the data' + better filtering to navigate/debug prompts. The old Recent-calls was a fixed top-15 glance with no pagination or filters, so most of 2,746 calls were unreachable. Grid filters down and each row links to the viewer to read the exact prompt/output. Free-text q searches id/client/purpose (not prompt body -- unindexed/large) to keep the query fast; pager is above the table so controls are always visible. Filter bar renders once and the table/pager refresh in place, so typing and auto-refresh never fight.

decision: Move storage + judgment-cache management (size on disk, prune, clear cache) off the dashboard into a dedicated /settings page; add a header nav link.
rationale: Ferosh: cache size/clear were hard to find (buried at the bottom of the dashboard below the now-25-row Calls grid) and suggested a separate settings page with the trace store. New /settings shows storage stats incl. judgment cache size (231 entries · 45 KB) with prune + clear-cache controls, plus a read-only provider chain. Home page decluttered to strip + providers + Calls grid. Static pages served per-request; only the PAGES route registration needed the restart.

decision: Decouple cache clearing from trace pruning: prune is traces-only (rejects cache flag), judgment cache gets its own POST /v1/admin/cache/clear; Settings page splits into separate Trace store and Judgment cache sections each with its own controls.
rationale: Ferosh flagged the shortcut: clear-cache had been bolted onto POST /v1/admin/prune via a {cache:true} flag and shared the prune button row, making 'older than 7d' read as ambiguous (trace vs cache). Fixed at the API level (dedicated endpoint, prune no longer accepts cache) and UI (two labeled sections, generic actionBtn targeting each endpoint). Docs updated. Test asserts separation: prune 400s on a cache flag; cache/clear reports count and leaves traces intact. NOTE: verification call cleared the live cache (231 entries) -- non-destructive, re-warms on next eval.
